# Step deck — Style Prompt

> A tips video as a numbered deck over a talking head. Every spoken word lands on screen on its onset, sized by how much it matters and set behind the speaker's head, so the head hides the lower part of the words. Between face shots the film cuts every 1–2 s to flat full-screen cards: navy word cards for questions and doubts, white word pages for statements, a quiet cream card with one icon in a black disk, black-and-white paper prints of the line's objects, line drawings. Each step opens on its own card with a giant italic numeral that shrinks into place, the colour field rotating navy, off-white, electric blue. A flat ending: the payoff lands on the face as the one gradient word of the film.

## 1. Essence, and what it is not

1. **Every spoken word lands on its onset.** A word appears on the frame it is spoken, at its final place in a phrase that was laid out first (the phrase grows in place), as a new caption state or as a sub-line. States swap hard. Nearly every frame carries text.
2. **Size is importance.** Each word gets a tier from what it carries: tiny for connectives, mid, big for the content word, a serif italic voice for the payoff or abstract word of a clause (about 1 in 6, never two in a row).
3. **On the face the words sit behind the head.** The caption layer lies between the footage and the speaker's cut-out; its baseline sits on the crown of the head. On cards the words are the graphic, centred.
4. **A new world every 1–2 s.** The face fills 35–45 % of the film and alternates with full-screen cards; cuts land on word onsets; the motion lives in the elements (push-backs, the shrinking numeral), never in a filter on the face.
5. **Every step opens on its own card** with a giant italic numeral, so the viewer always knows where they are in the list.

Not a slideshow of bullet points (no lists of text, one state at a time). Not a kinetic-type film on a solid colour (the face comes back every few seconds). Not a meme edit (no emoji, no reaction sounds, no shake). No comment-keyword call to action, no end card, no em dashes on screen.

## 2. Materials & rendering

- **The face**: the user's talking-head clip from `list_media`, full bleed, as shot (no grade, no filter). The caption layer for face worlds sits ABOVE the clip and BELOW a cut-out of the speaker: run `make_cutout` on the face windows (≤ 6 s each) and place the `cut_…webm` as a second `<video>` with the cutout timing rule (`data-start = S + max(0, from − M)`, `data-media-start = max(0, M − from)`), so the head covers the words. Without a cut-out, put the words above the head and drop the overlap. Reframe a horizontal clip to 9:16 around the face (craft `reframe.md`).
- **Word timing**: take the words from `inspect_media` (`words: [{text, start, end}]`) and land each word on its `start`; check names and prices with the user.
- **Cards**: flat colour fields, no texture, no shadow except a soft drop shadow under step words on a dark field. The navy card is `--utama`, the white page `--latar`, the cream icon card `--latar-2`, the third step `--aksen`.
- **Prints**: objects (never people) as black-and-white photocopies (steep curve, crushed blacks) on a 70–90 % wide paper card with a slight tilt and sometimes a black bar along the top, on paper white, swapped on a ~10 fps clock (holds 2, 3, 3, 4, 3 … frames) with 1–3 px jitter. Real photos from the user go through the same grayscale + contrast.
- **Line drawings** on the white page: 5 px strokes in `--teks`, missing parts dashed at 30 %, each part popping on its word while the rest goes soft.
- **The cream icon card**: a black disk r 113 at the centre with one drawn icon inside in the card colour, tiny words hugging it above and below; the icon empties or changes on twos.
- The example paints a stand-in talking head once (room with bokeh, the person on a separate layer); replace both with the user's clip and its cut-out.

## 3. Colour logic

- `--utama` is the navy field: question and doubt cards, Step 1. Words on it use `--teks-di-utama` (the warm off-white).
- `--latar` is the white page: statements, drawings, Step 2. Words in `--teks`; the faint numeral is `--teks` mixed 20 % into the page.
- `--aksen` is the electric blue: Step 3 and a box under a winning noun. Words in `--teks-di-aksen`.
- `--latar-2` is the cream icon card, ink in `--teks`.
- The numeral is always a quiet tint of its field (34–36 % of the word colour mixed into the field), never a loud colour.
- Fixed in every brand: the face captions (`--cap`, near white with a soft 35 % black glow, never an outline or a pill), the paper white and red of the hook montage (`--kertas`, `--merah`, red only on those words), and the one gradient word (`--g1`…`--g5`, orange → pink → violet → blue), used once per film on the payoff, behind the head.
- A dark brand turns the white page dark with light words; the rotation still reads as three different fields.

## 4. Type

- `--font-judul` carries the content words at 600 with −0.04 em tracking: face tiers M 112 px and B 150 px (a line shrinks to fit 930 px, never under 56 px); card tiers M 150, B 170. Inter suits; any grotesk at 600 works.
- `--font-isi` carries the tiny tier at 600: 64 px on the face, 68 px on cards (never smaller).
- The serif voice is Playfair Display Italic 400: 170 px on the face, 178 px on cards, and the giant step numerals (about 1,300 px font size, 960 px tall, centred slightly left of the frame centre).
- The red montage words: `--font-judul` 800, 240 px, −0.05 em. The gradient payoff word: Poppins 800, 196 px.
- Sentence case everywhere; tracking tight; one space = 0.26 em between word boxes.

## 5. Motion quality

- 30 fps. Hard cuts on word onsets. A world lasts 1–2 s on average and never more than ~4.6 s; the hook stack (three worlds) fits the first 3–6 s.
- **First word of a face world**: fades over 6 frames (0 → .11 → .51 → .80 → .91 → .96 → 1) and rises 30 px, `power2.out`. Every other word appears in one frame.
- **Push-back** on entry: the opening caption layer 1.36 → 1 in 0.6 s `circ.out`, then a linear drift to 0.95; montage 1.36 → 1 in 0.6 s, each red word 1.22 → 1 in 0.3 s; card words 1.25 → 1 in 1.04 s `circ.out`.
- **Step card**: the numeral enters at ×1.48 with blur 14 / 6 / 3 / 0 px over 4 frames and shrinks `circ.out` in 0.88 s, then drifts linearly; a 10-frame glow on the field steps down hard.
- **Flicker-on** for one stressed word: 6 stepped opacity keys a frame apart (light: .84 .14 .32 .14 .46 1; dark or keyword: .85 .30 .65 .35 .80 1).
- **Push-out** from a card back to the face: the card leaves left `power2.in` in 0.35–0.75 s, the next caption layer enters from x +400 `circ.out` 1.24 s.
- At most one punch-in (×1.20, scale only) per film. Nothing moves or filters the face otherwise.

## 6. Camera grammar

| Move | What it expresses | Can serve |
|---|---|---|
| Push-back ×1.36 → 1, `circ.out` 0.6 s | a new world arrives with weight | the first face world, the montage, every card |
| Linear drift (×1.05–1.15 over the world) | keep the still frame alive | cards, step numerals |
| Numeral shrink ×1.48 → 1 with a blur ramp | "here is step N" | each step of a list |
| Flicker-on (6 stepped keys) | the word the speaker leans on | a doubt, a twist, the payoff |
| Push-out left + caption layer in from the right | back to the face after a run of cards | chapter ends |
| Exit to white (brighten + blur over 7 frames) | into a picture | the one metaphor clip |
| One punch-in ×1.20 | the clause the speaker leans on | once per film |
| Hard cut on the onset | the default | everything else |

## 7. Native moves

- **Words behind the head.** The phrase is laid out first, centred on x 540; each word appears on its onset; the head covers the lower part. *Fits content like:* "Foto produkmu kok kusam?" for a shop; a creator's "Tiga kesalahan editing"; a teacher's "Rumus ini sering salah"; a storyteller's "Malam itu hujan".
- **Hook stack.** Three worlds for the first three lines: the face with the first word big, a loud world of B&W prints flickering with red words, a quiet cream card with tiny words around one icon. *Fits content like:* "HP baru. Lampu. Filter." then "tetap saja gelap"; a kitchen's "Garam. Gula. Api." then "tetap hambar"; a student's "Les. Buku. Video." then "tetap lupa".
- **Step card.** A full field (navy, off-white, blue in turn), a giant italic numeral shrinking into place, the step's words on top, the first word sharpening. *Fits content like:* a recipe's three steps; three habits of a freelancer; three rules of a board game; the three acts of a short story.
- **Navy doubt card.** A question or a turn on navy, the phrase growing in place, one word flickering on. *Fits content like:* "Masalahnya bukan di kamera"; "Tapi apakah perlu mahal?"; "Siapa yang salah?".
- **Drawing page.** A line drawing of the line's nouns; each part draws on its word, the one being said stays sharp, the rest fades back; a missing part dashed until it is named. *Fits content like:* a phone above a plate with a reflector; a desk setup; a seating plan; a family tree.
- **The gradient word.** Once per film, the payoff word in the orange → blue gradient behind the head, flickering on and rising 24 px, then held. *Fits content like:* "terang."; "laku."; "lulus."; "pulang.".

## 8. Pitfalls

- Words in front of the face: the caption layer must sit between the clip and its cut-out, baseline on the crown (+14 px for big words, −38 px for tiny ones). Never over the eyes or the mouth.
- Two serif words in a row, or a serif word every line: the voice loses its weight. About 1 in 6.
- Fading or sliding every word: only the first word of a face world fades; the rest pop in one frame.
- A grade, blur or black-and-white on the speaker: black and white is for prints only.
- More than one gradient word, red outside the hook montage, or a coloured numeral that shouts over its words.
- Worlds longer than ~4.6 s, or a card run with no face for more than ~6 s.
- Caption words under 56 px; anything in the top 220 px or under y 1500 except a push-back's first frames.
- An end card, a "comment KATA" call to action, a pen outro: the film ends on the payoff word.

## Measured from the references

- Face on screen 38–41 % of the film; 29 worlds in 63 s (a new world every ~2.2 s, never over ~4.6 s); nearly every frame (97 %) carries text.
- Caption tiers on the face: T 64, M 112, B 152, S 170, gradient 200 px; on cards T 68, M 150, B 170, S 178; the line fits 930 px; baseline on the crown with offsets T −38, M −10, B/S +14, gradient +26 px.
- Step numeral 960 px tall centred at (523, 946) of 1080 × 1920; numeral ×1.48 → 1 in 0.88 s `circ.out` with a 14/6/3/0 px blur ramp; step words ×1.25 → 1 in 1.04 s; drift ×1.156 over the card.
- Montage holds 2–4 frames per print (~10 fps), push-backs 1.36 and 1.22.
- Sound (for placing sound effects): 3.6–4.3 effects per 10 s, only where a world changes or something enters; whooshes start 3–10 frames before the cut, hits on the cut frame, nothing on caption swaps, the payoff quiet.

# Step deck: beat plan

Default length 15 s. Tempo per beat (seconds): short 1.0, medium 1.4, long 2.2.

## hook

- en: stack of three worlds: the face with the first word big behind the head, a B&W print flicker with red words, a quiet cream icon card
- id: tiga dunia bertumpuk: wajah dengan kata besar di belakang kepala, cetakan hitam-putih berkedip dengan kata merah, kartu krem sunyi

## problem

- en: the doubt on a navy word card, the phrase growing in place, one word flickering on; then the face with the serif word behind the head
- id: keraguan di kartu kata navy, frasa tumbuh di tempat, satu kata berkedip; lalu wajah dengan kata serif di belakang kepala

## fact

- en: a statement on a white word page, words landing on their onsets, sized by importance, the abstract word in serif italic
- id: pernyataan di halaman kata putih, tiap kata mendarat saat diucapkan, besarnya menurut pentingnya, kata abstrak serif miring

## step

- en: one full-screen step card per step, navy, white, blue in turn: a giant italic numeral shrinks into place, the step's words on top
- id: satu kartu penuh per langkah, bergantian navy, putih, biru: angka miring raksasa menyusut ke tempatnya, kata langkah di atasnya

## compare

- en: two line drawings on the white page, the one being said sharp, the other faded back; a blue box under the winning noun
- id: dua gambar garis di halaman putih, yang sedang disebut tajam, yang lain surut; kotak biru di bawah kata yang menang

## number

- en: a counter on the white page, one value per frame, then the words land one per line under it
- id: penghitung di halaman putih, satu angka per frame, lalu katanya mendarat satu per baris di bawahnya

## proof

- en: B&W paper prints of the line's objects on a 10 fps clock, the proof word big in red over them
- id: cetakan kertas hitam-putih benda dalam kalimat, berganti 10 fps, kata buktinya besar merah di atasnya

## offer

- en: a navy word card naming the offer, the price as the serif word, the phrase growing in place
- id: kartu kata navy menyebut tawarannya, harga sebagai kata serif, frasa tumbuh di tempat

## cta

- en: the face, the ask behind the head, the handle as a small sub-line; held 2 s, no end card
- id: wajah, ajakannya di belakang kepala, nama akun sebagai baris kecil; diam 2 dtk, tanpa kartu penutup

## payoff

- en: the face with the one gradient word of the film behind the head, flickering on and rising; held flat to the end
- id: wajah dengan satu-satunya kata bergradasi di belakang kepala, berkedip lalu naik; diam datar sampai habis

         --latar = halaman putih, --latar-2 = kartu krem, --utama = kartu navy (langkah 1), --aksen = biru listrik (langkah 3). */

        --g1: #ff6a2b; --g2: #ff2d7a; --g3: #c04ae0; --g4: #6e7cff; --g5: #5a9bff;

      }
      * { margin: 0; padding: 0; box-sizing: border-box; }

      #root { position: relative; width: 100%; height: 100%; overflow: hidden; background: var(--latar); color: var(--teks); font-family: var(--font-isi); }
      .full, .full img { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; width: 1080px; height: 1920px; }
      /* Rekaman: ruangan, lalu lapisan caption, lalu orangnya (= matte/cutout), jadi kepala menutup bagian bawah kata. */
      #wajah, #orang { transform-origin: 540px 1000px; }
      #fitur { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; width: 1080px; height: 1920px; overflow: visible; }
      .mata { fill: var(--f-rambut); } .alis { fill: none; stroke: var(--f-rambut); stroke-width: 9; stroke-linecap: round; }

      .G { font: 800 196px/1 "Poppins", var(--font-judul); letter-spacing: -0.03em; padding: 0 8px;

      .biru .angka { color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--teks-di-aksen) 36%, var(--aksen)); }
